question.problem:
Find the solution to the following initial value problem.

$$
{\begin{aligned}{x}_{1}^{′}(t)=4{x}_{1}(t)+{x}_{2}(t) \\ {x}_{2}^{′}(t)=-{x}_{2}(t),\end{aligned}\,x(0)=[\begin{aligned}-1 \\ 10\end{aligned}]
$$
question.worked_solution:
First, we write down the matrix differential equation ${x}^{′}(t)=Ax(t)$ for the given system:

$$
[\begin{aligned}{x}_{1}^{′}(t) \\ {x}_{2}^{′}(t)\end{aligned}]=[\begin{aligned}4 & 1 \\ 0 & -1\end{aligned}][\begin{aligned}{x}_{1}(t) \\ {x}_{2}(t)\end{aligned}]
$$

We need to find the eigenvalues and the eigenvectors of the matrix $A.$

- Since $A$ is upper-triangular, the eigenvalues are 

$$
{\lambda }_{1}=4\,\text{and}\,{\lambda }_{2}=-1.
$$

- Let's go through the process of finding the eigenvectors.

- For ${\lambda }_{1}=4,$ we get 

$$
A-{\lambda }_{1}I=[\begin{aligned}0 & 1 \\ 0 & -5\end{aligned}]∼[\begin{aligned}0 & 1 \\ 0 & 0\end{aligned}].
$$

So, we get an eigenvector 
${v}_{1}=[\begin{aligned}1 \\ 0\end{aligned}].$

- For ${\lambda }_{2}=-1,$ we get 

$$
A-{\lambda }_{2}I=[\begin{aligned}5 & 1 \\ 0 & 0\end{aligned}].
$$

So, we get an eigenvector 
${v}_{2}=[\begin{aligned}-1 \\ 5\end{aligned}].$

Now, we write down the general solution to the given linear system of differential equations:

$$
\begin{aligned}x(t) & ={c}_{1}{v}_{1}{e}^{{\lambda }_{1}t}+{c}_{2}{v}_{2}{e}^{{\lambda }_{2}t} \\  & ={c}_{1}[\begin{aligned}1 \\ 0\end{aligned}]{e}^{4t}+{c}_{2}[\begin{aligned}-1 \\ 5\end{aligned}]{e}^{-t},\,{c}_{1},{c}_{2}\in R\end{aligned}
$$

Next, we find the values of ${c}_{1}$ and ${c}_{2}.$ Substituting $t=0$ into the general solution, we get the following:

$$
\begin{aligned}x(0) & =[\begin{aligned}-1 \\ 10\end{aligned}] \\ {c}_{1}[\begin{aligned}1 \\ 0\end{aligned}]{e}^{4(0)}+{c}_{2}[\begin{aligned}-1 \\ 5\end{aligned}]{e}^{-0} & =[\begin{aligned}-1 \\ 10\end{aligned}] \\ {c}_{1}[\begin{aligned}1 \\ 0\end{aligned}]+{c}_{2}[\begin{aligned}-1 \\ 5\end{aligned}] & =[\begin{aligned}-1 \\ 10\end{aligned}] \\ [\begin{aligned}{c}_{1}-{c}_{2} \\ 5{c}_{2}\end{aligned}] & =[\begin{aligned}-1 \\ 10\end{aligned}]\end{aligned}
$$

So, we have a system of linear equations

$$
{\begin{aligned}{c}_{1}-{c}_{2}=-1 \\ 5{c}_{2}=10.\end{aligned}
$$

From the second equation, we get ${c}_{2}=2.$ Substituting into the first equation, we obtain ${c}_{1}=1.$ 

Finally, we write down the solution to the initial value problem:

$$
\begin{aligned}x(t) & =[\begin{aligned}1 \\ 0\end{aligned}]{e}^{4t}+2[\begin{aligned}-1 \\ 5\end{aligned}]{e}^{-t}\end{aligned}
$$
